title: Single derived-unit formula in a proper/open tower
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, j:X→U, b:U→Xbar and i:Y→Ybar open immersions of schemes, q:U→Y, p:Xbar→Ybar and s:Ybar→Z any morphisms. Let J,I,M be complexes on X,U,Xbar, with I,M K-injective, u:j_!J→I and v:b_!I→M quasi-isomorphisms. Let χ:i_!q_*≅p_*b_! be any natural isomorphism. Put t=v∘b_!u and a=j then b. The class of s_*p_*t∘s_*χ at j_!J equals the following single-unit expression: apply s_*χ; use s_*p_*≅(p then s)_* and b_!j_!≅a_!; apply the total derived unit for (p then s)_*; apply its derived image of the total augmentation a_!J→M; identify the value at M by the inverse unit on M; finally undo the direct-image composition at M. These are precisely the canonical natural isomorphisms, not arbitrary choices. Complexes and localization are as in [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], open composition as in [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. The attached Lean statement spells out the complete equality.

proof.text: For any chain map h:K→M with M K-injective, naturality of the total-right-derived unit gives η_K;R(Qh);η_M⁻¹=Q(t_*h). This follows by postcomposing naturality with the invertible unit at M. No assumption that direct image preserves quasi-isomorphisms is used.

Apply the preceding identity to the total augmentation a_!J→M. Expand the augmentation using the canonical open-composition isomorphism [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. Its forward and inverse maps cancel. Naturality of the underived direct-image composition transports b_!u;v across the comparison, and its forward and inverse components at M cancel. Functoriality of Q gives exactly the stated equality.

theorem properOpenTowerSingleUnitFormula
    (J : CochainComplex (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) ℤ)
    (I : CochainComplex (Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) ℤ)
    (M : CochainComplex (Sheaf Xbar.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) ℤ)
    [I.IsKInjective] [M.IsKInjective]
    (u : (((j)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj J ⟶ I)
    (v : (((b)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj I ⟶ M)
    [QuasiIso u] [QuasiIso v]
    (χ : ((q)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]) ⋙ ((i)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]) ≅
      ((b)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]) ⋙ ((p)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]))
    : let jc := ((j)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
      let bc := ((b)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
      let pc := ((p)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
      let sc := ((s)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
      let tc := ((p ≫ s)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
      let e := NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex
        (openImmersionLowerShriekComp (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j b) (.up ℤ)
      let d := NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex
        (lowerStarComp (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) p s) (.up ℤ)
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (sc.map ((NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex χ.hom (.up ℤ)).app
        (jc.obj J)) ≫ sc.map (pc.map (bc.map u ≫ v))) =
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (sc.map ((NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex χ.hom (.up ℤ)).app
        (jc.obj J))) ≫
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (d.hom.app (bc.obj (jc.obj J))) ≫
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (tc.map (e.inv.app J)) ≫
      ((p ≫ s)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]).rightDerivedFunctorUnit.app
        ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj
          ((((j ≫ b)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj J)) ≫
      R((p ≫ s)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]).map
        (DerivedCategory.Q.map (e.hom.app J ≫ bc.map u ≫ v)) ≫
      (((p ≫ s)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]).rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso M).hom ≫
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (d.inv.app M)
